The lifespan perspective emphasizes that development is a lifelong process involving both growth and decline at all stages, not just gains in youth and losses in old age.  
Option (A) incorrectly restricts gains to youth and losses to old age.  
Option (B) correctly reflects that at every age, some capacities improve while others may decline.  
Option (C) is too extreme — not every gain is offset by an equal loss; there can be net gains or losses in different domains.  
Option (D) incorrectly prioritizes gains over losses, whereas the lifespan perspective treats them as equally important parts of development.  

Final answer: (B)
